problem: RL agents that learn from raw RGB observations have weak perception of objects, so they are inefficient at finding and interacting with target objects. Prior work rarely combines large vision foundation models such as SAM and YOLOv5 with RL agents.
motivation: Object interaction needs precise recognition, localization and segmentation of objects. Pre-trained foundation models generalize across domains and reduce the need for task-specific data. The paper's premise is that feeding their outputs into a PPO agent's observation will improve interaction and navigation.
key_idea: Run frozen YOLOv5 to detect objects, prompt SAM with the boxes to get masks, encode the boxes, classes and masks with a CNN, and use the result as the state of a PPO agent in AI2-THOR.
insight: The only evidence is a comparison of the full perception-enhanced agent against a raw-RGB PPO baseline, which shows large gains on every metric. There is no ablation separating the effect of YOLOv5, SAM or the feature encoding, so the paper does not show which part matters. The gains are also not tested on unseen scenes, so generalization is unverified.
method: YOLOv5 detection: frozen YOLOv5 runs on the RGB frame and outputs bounding boxes B and class labels C.
SAM segmentation: the YOLOv5 boxes are used as prompts to frozen SAM, which produces instance masks M.
Feature encoding: a CNN encodes (B, C, M) into a state representation phi(s_t).
Reward: r_t = alpha*(d_{t-1}-d_t) + beta*success - gamma*collision/invalid-action penalty, with weights tuned empirically.
Policy network: a CNN perception encoder feeds two fully connected heads that output action probabilities and state value.
PPO training: clipped surrogate objective, lr 3e-4, gamma 0.99, GAE lambda 0.95, clip 0.2, batch 64, 4 epochs, 1e6 steps, 5 seeds.

setting.backbone: PPO agent with a CNN encoder and FC heads, trained from scratch, on top of frozen YOLOv5 and frozen SAM
setting.training_data: RL interaction in 4 AI2-THOR kitchen scenes (FloorPlan1-4), 1e6 steps; YOLOv5 and SAM are pre-trained and not fine-tuned
setting.observation: egocentric first-person RGB, processed into YOLOv5 boxes/classes and SAM masks
setting.action_space: discrete: MoveAhead, RotateLeft, RotateRight, LookUp, LookDown, PickupObject, DropObject
setting.privileged: The reward uses the distance to the target object, which is training-time information. At test time, the target object is specified at the start of each episode.

numbers.backbone: PPO with frozen YOLOv5 + SAM features
numbers.extra: averaged over 4 kitchen scenes and 5 seeds; the same scenes are used for training and evaluation, and the paper does not state a separate held-out split
numbers.evidence: Table 1: Performance comparison of agents across all four environments; Success Rate (%) 73.5 ± 2.1, Avg. Cumulative Reward 136.4 ± 5.6, Navigation Efficiency (%) 82.1 ± 1.9, Interaction Efficiency 1.2 ± 0.1

numbers_note: Only a single aggregated table was given. There are no per-scene numbers and no standard navigation benchmarks. The text claims a 52.5% relative success-rate improvement, a 68.2% reward improvement and a 33.1% navigation-efficiency improvement.
results: The perception-enhanced agent reaches 73.5% success versus 48.2% for the raw-RGB PPO baseline. Average cumulative reward rises from 81.1 to 136.4 and navigation efficiency from 61.7% to 82.1%. Interaction attempts fall from 2.1 to 1.2. The only baseline is the same PPO agent without SAM/YOLOv5.
limitations: The evaluation is in only four kitchen scenes, with no unseen-scene test and no ablation of YOLOv5 versus SAM.
The only baseline is a raw-RGB PPO agent, with no comparison to other detection- or segmentation-based RL or navigation methods.
Computational overhead is discussed only qualitatively, with no runtime numbers, and the method is simulation-only.
compares_to: Standard PPO agent with raw RGB observations
